title: 22-Layer ZnS/MgF2 with Bounded Thickness and Optical-Path Smoothness Penalty
scientific_hypothesis: Constraining layer thicknesses to 700-1100 nm range while penalizing optical-path differences between adjacent layers will suppress the 1200+ nm excursions observed in prior iterations, yielding smoother phase progression across the stack while maintaining dual-band transmittance performance for CH4 and CO2 sensing bands.
design_principle: Alternating high-low index quarter-wave stack with thickness bounds informed by prior iteration deviations. Optical-path smoothness penalty enforces gradual phase accumulation rather than abrupt thickness jumps that complicate deposition control.
proposed_topology: Air | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | CaF2 substrate. Total 22 finite layers.
design_variables: All 22 layer thicknesses bounded to [700, 1100] nm
Optical-path difference penalty weight in loss function
soft_objectives: Maximize mean transmittance in 3250-3350 nm band
Maximize mean transmittance in 4200-4300 nm band
Minimize mean transmittance in 2500-3100 nm band
Minimize mean transmittance in 4450-5000 nm band
Minimize thickness excursion beyond 700-1100 nm bounds
Minimize optical-path difference between adjacent layer pairs
manufacturing_considerations: Thickness bounds 700-1100 nm avoid extreme deposition times
ZnS and MgF2 are conventional depositable IR dielectrics
theory_basis: Transfer matrix method for coherent multilayer interference
Quarter-wave stack principle for bandpass filter construction
Optical-path smoothness reduces deposition stress and thickness control errors
expected_advantages: Suppresses 1200+ nm thickness excursions seen in iterations 01, 09, 13
Enforces smoother phase progression across stack
Maintains 22-layer count that achieved 0.955 target score in iteration 01
Bounds are physically motivated by prior observation, not arbitrary
known_risks: Tighter bounds may limit optimizer's ability to find global optimum
Smoothness penalty may conflict with dual-band resonance requirements
ZnS absorption may increase at longer wavelengths
execution_request_english: Optimize a 22-layer planar multilayer filter on CaF2 substrate under air incidence. Stack sequence: ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2 (22 finite layers total). All layer thicknesses bounded to [700, 1100] nm. Optimize for high mean transmittance in 3250-3350 nm and 4200-4300 nm passbands, low mean transmittance in 2500-3100 nm and 4450-5000 nm stopbands. Include optical-path difference penalty in loss function to suppress thickness excursions and enforce smooth phase progression. Use gradient-based thickness optimizer with coherent TMM solver. Normal unpolarized illumination. No metal layers. Evaluate all 22 thicknesses as continuous design variables. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 2500-3100 nm, 3250-3350 nm, 4200-4300 nm, 4450-5000 nm. soft objectives: High transmittance in 3.25-3.35 um and 4.20-4.30 um bands; Low transmittance in 2.50-3.10 um and 4.45-5.00 um bands. behaviors to suppress or avoid: High transmittance in 2.50-3.10 um and 4.45-5.00 um bands. manufacturing constraints: Total layer count <= 24; No metal layers; Conventional depositable infrared inorganic dielectric materials only.
revision_reason: Refines route_01 based on feedback directive to constrain thickness search to 700-1100 nm and introduce optical-path difference penalty. Prior iterations showed thickness excursions beyond 1200 nm (iteration 01: 1601 nm, 1865 nm; iteration 09: 1575 nm, 1506 nm; iteration 13: 1249 nm). This revision directly addresses those deviations while preserving the 22-layer topology that achieved highest target score (0.955) in iteration 01.
